action.rationale: The Java version is unknown; verify the deployed runtime before selecting a PQC API baseline.
steps: Target JDK 24+ for ML-KEM and ML-DSA support planning.
Pilot compatibility testing in CI before production migration.
action.title: Check Java runtime baseline for standard PQC APIs

action.rationale: BouncyCastle can be used as a pragmatic transition option when standard runtime support is unavailable or incomplete.
steps: Verify the resolved BC release and deployed JDK support before provider initialization; the example uses BC Java 1.85 and the BC provider, not BCPQC.

Select explicit ML-DSA / ML-KEM parameter sets for the intended purpose. Generate new algorithm-compatible keys and provision matching public keys and encodings to verifiers; never reuse RSA key material.
Document provider ordering and FIPS/compliance impact.
action.title: Provide BouncyCastle PQC fallback path

action.rationale: PKI updates require coordinated CA, chain, and relying-party compatibility planning. FIPS 204/205 standardize signature primitives, not a universal hybrid certificate format.
steps: Inventory certificate signature algorithms and key sizes from CBOM/report output.
Identify the exact certificate construction and encoding, then verify provider, CA, client and trust-store support before planning issuance.
Pilot only a supported construction in non-production trust stores; if format or ecosystem support is unavailable, keep issuance unverified and evaluate another supported migration path.
Define reissuance plan for quantum-vulnerable roots/intermediates/end-entity certs.
action.title: Plan certificate algorithm and trust-store migration

action.rationale: Modern JDKs expose standardized PQC algorithm names through JCA, reducing vendor lock-in.
steps: Select an explicit parameter set and generate a new ML-DSA key pair; never reuse RSA key material.
Provision matching public keys and required JOSE/PKI encodings to all verifiers before switching signers to ML-DSA where policy allows.
Adopt ML-KEM for key establishment in hybrid TLS/key exchange designs.
Keep dual verification during migration to preserve compatibility.
action.title: Use Java standard JCA names for ML-DSA / ML-KEM

action.rationale: Envoy TLS behavior depends on configured providers and peer capabilities; PQC signature readiness can vary between mesh edges, sidecars, and external clients.
steps: Harden min/max TLS versions and retire static RSA key exchange where configured; ECDHE_RSA uses RSA authentication, not static RSA key exchange.
Review cipher_suites for TLS 1.0-1.2, not TLS 1.3; review certificate signatures and peer compatibility separately.
Verify PQC certificate-signature compatibility in both downstream and upstream clusters.
Gate production rollout with staged canary tests and explicit fallback paths.
action.title: Validate Envoy PQC signature compatibility in control/data planes

action.rationale: Envoy control-plane config supports strict min/max protocol and cipher suite policy.
steps: Prefer `tls_minimum_protocol_version: TLSv1_3`; use TLSv1_2 only when interoperability requires it.
Review `cipher_suites` for TLS 1.0-1.2, not TLS 1.3. Retire static RSA key exchange where configured; ECDHE_RSA uses RSA authentication, not static RSA key exchange.
Review certificate-signature migration and peer compatibility separately before removing RSA authentication.
action.title: Set modern TLS policy in Envoy
